newsitem.title: JORDAN: Hamas urges Arafat to join "new intifada".
newsitem.headline: Hamas urges Arafat to join "new intifada".

text.p: The Islamic movement Hamas urged Yasser Arafat on Thursday to join the "new intifada" or uprising against Israel, saying two days of bloody clashes with Israeli soldiers showed Palestinians were ready to die for their rights.
Hamas spokesman Ibrahim Ghosheh said Palestinians had turned their backs on a 1993 Oslo self-rule deal Arafat signed with Israel which had brought them only greater suffering.
More than 30 people have been killed in the fighting, sparked by Israel's opening of a tunnel close to a Moslem sanctuary in Jerusalem.

"(The fact that) many Palestinians were killed...gives an answer to everyone who thinks the Palestinans have been calmed down by the Oslo agreement," Ghosheh told Reuters. "Palestinians ...want their land and they are ready to give their lives."

He said the 1993 accord, under which Palestinians took over limited authority in the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank, had tightened an Israeli stranglehold over Palestinians and created apartheid-style cantons in their territories.

"See now how Palestinian leaders like Arafat are frustrated, disappointed. They didn't get anything," Ghosheh said. "The (Jewish) settlements keep growing, Palestinians are forbidden from going to Jerusalem to pray in the Aqsa mosque...(and) live in allocated areas like what happened in South Africa."

"With the new intifada which started today one can read that the Palestinians have decided to recontinue their resistance to occupation. We hope (Arafat) will follow the route of the Palestinian people, of resistance, and the route of the intifada," he added.
Further talks between Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would be fruitless, Ghosheh said.
"He knows he will get nothing from Netanyahu. He will get words, big words."
